sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: vision testers and forms, blood alcohol thresholds, test refusal and drug types
Confusable pairs among vision screening routes, blood alcohol thresholds, refusal penalties and drug categories, followed by continuation facts; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
Bioptic telescopic lens users file the Low Vision Acuity Screening, form 412-LV, with the SCDMV Driver Improvement unit every year, so their screening is an annual filing. [A01]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable form four-twelve-LV versus four-twelve-NC.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A02
A South Carolina-licensed eye care professional must submit the Certificate of Vision Examination electronically through SCDMV's online portal, whereas an out-of-state professional must complete SCDMV Form four-twelve-NC [A02].
Why it matters: group vision; confusable in-state versus out-of-state professional.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A02
Corrective lens restriction code A is added when lenses are needed to meet the minimum standard, and removing it requires a vision screening. [A02]
Why it matters: group vision; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
Branch testing is optional: you may skip it and go straight to a licensed eye care professional, who must also test you if you fail the branch test. [A02]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable optional choice versus required after failure.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A04
The SC phone law targets devices that need the use of either hand while driving, rather than every possible phone use. [A04]
Why it matters: group distraction; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A04
Distracted driving can cause collisions with injury, death or property damage, and the driver remains responsible for operating the vehicle safely. [A04]
Why it matters: group distraction; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A05
Speeding and tailgating are listed as aggressive behaviors, and so is failing to obey stop signs, yield signs, traffic signals or railroad crossing signals. [A05]
Why it matters: group aggression; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A06
A BAC of 0.15 percent or more is a suspension trigger, a BAC of 0.05 can still support an impaired-driving conviction, and 0.02 is where vision is already affected. [A06]
Why it matters: group alcohol; confusable fifteen hundredths versus five hundredths versus two hundredths.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A06
The manual's best advice is not to drive any vehicle after drinking alcohol or using other drugs, and never to let a friend or relative drive after drinking. [A06]
Why it matters: group alcohol; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A07
An alcohol concentration test is usually done by breath, blood or urine, and a police officer may require all three under implied consent. [A07]
Why it matters: group alcohol; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A08
Prescription and illegal drugs can both affect reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness in ways similar to alcohol. [A08]
Why it matters: group drugs; confusable legal versus illegal drugs.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A08
The manual says no one can drink alcohol or use other impairing drugs and still drive safely. [A08]
Why it matters: group drugs; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A09
Extreme levels of any emotion, not only anger, can keep you from driving well, and staying off the road until symptoms pass is the safest choice. [A09]
Why it matters: group emotions; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A09
Older drivers may not have the same ability to act quickly in an emergency as before, because physical dexterity may weaken with age. [A09]
Why it matters: group older drivers; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A10
For health concerns about driving the manual advises talking with a doctor, who may decide your driving skills should be assessed by an SCDMV examiner or a trained medical professional. [A10]
Why it matters: group older drivers; difficulty medium.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0041]

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
